schoolReviews.review: Gullett's outdoor space is one of its biggest strengths. As a school park shared with Parks and Rec, it has a real community feel, well-used and clearly loved by the neighborhood, not just by families at the school. Kids spend genuine time outside gardening among mature trees and garden beds, rather than being stuck on the shadeless concrete lots so many campuses have. The historic building only adds to the character; while newer schools often feel like sealed-off office fortresses, Gullett feels woven into the community around it. The teachers match that spirit too: patient, caring, and just as focused on kids' social-emotional growth as on academics.

Gullett is such a sweet school. The family involvement is great and everybody tries to take care of each other. The teachers have been great so far. Every classroom has a garden which is so fun and educational. Academics seem high, and I really like the principal, you can tell she really cares about the school absolutely the kids.

I can't say enough good things about Gullett. The entire experience is one of engagement and togetherness. My kids love it. The teachers are, shockingly, happy and engaged as well. I feel lucky we found it and lucky our kids get to go there.
Gullett is a great school. The teachers are amazing the family engagement is over the top. My children have very much enjoyed their time at Gullet.

Gullett is a welcoming, creative and lovely school that truly feels like a part of the neighborhood community. We've been sending our kids there since 2015 - and have been so happy with the experience!
The best space for my kids. They love coming to school, the community is wonderful and overall Gullett shares a lot of the same values we do in our home.

Gullett has been such a gift to our family. We have had school experiences that left us feeling discouraged and my kids feeling negatively about themselves. The staff and administration at Gullett have been incredibly supportive and energetic in engaging all of the kids. They have taken seriously and resolved any concerns we have raised in our child's special education plans. The school supports its teachers and families.

schoolReviews.review: This is my first year of middle her and my mental health dropped greatly due to pressure and too much homework, there were some great teachers but others were rude to me. kids here often did not get into fights but emotionally I feel the school isn't too welcome. kids there can relentlessly be mean to people and often get away with it. on the flip side, the fine Arts programs are really immersive and even though I don't necessarily enjoy learning, most of the core subject teachers definitely prepare you for the STAAR tests over all this is a mediocre school.

Our family has been part of the Lamar Middle School community for just over a month, and I want to acknowledge how much has improved since our initial concerns. The teachers, counselors, and many parents continue to be the highlight of our experience. They are caring, attentive, and genuinely dedicated to students’ learning and well-being.After sharing concerns about safety and bullying, I recently met with an administrator, Mr. Phelps, and counselors, Owens and Sheridan, and I could not have asked for a more compassionate and professional response. They listened carefully, addressed each issue with sincerity, and made clear commitments to supporting my daughter. Their collaboration and follow-through have helped rebuild my confidence that the school is taking these matters seriously.It’s clear that the counseling team and Mr. Phelps are working hard to ensure students feel safe, valued, and supported. I especially appreciate the warmth and respect they brought to our meeting. It reflected the best of what public education can be when respectful communication and empathy are prioritized.While every school can continue improving in areas like consistency and front office communication, our most recent experience shows that Lamar’s staff truly care and are responsive when families raise concerns. We are grateful for their time, professionalism, and commitment to student well-being.

AGHHHH I HATE THIS  I GOT SKIBIDI FANUM TAXED AT THIS SCHOOL I HATE THIS SCHOOL THIS SCHOOL MAKES MY BULKAN RAGE

I have lived in Austin for 16 years now. I have an almost 12 year old and this year is our first year in middle school. I have been amazed by the schools efforts to support the children as they transition from 5th grade to their middle school years. Socially and emotionally the school is on top of things. The principal is the true star here. I know a lot of teachers who are very grateful for his presence at the school. Also, its a Fine Arts Academy meaning your child has the option to excel in a major if they choose. My daughter has loved the technical theatre program. Its given her an opportunity to meet friends interested in things she is as well. Overall very impressed with all staff.

My daughter attended for part of a year. She loved her teachers. But she was bullied mercilessly and with witnesses and the bullies didn’t appear to feel repercussions and continued. She had to be the one to leave.

My son attended Lamar for two years. He was physically attacked multiple times. EMS was called once. There were at least four different principals during that time. He was threatened by a gang. He was fearful and refused to return. We removed him mid year.On the plus side, his math teacher recognized and promoted his talent.

Do not attend this school for music. The orchestra director is not skilled and places students with lots of experience with those that have little to no experience. My daughter was bored and asked to move, was faced with nothing but obstruction. I feel she was trying to stack the deck in her lower orchestra for UIL competition, so she did not want to move her. It was very upsetting. Principal is very unhelpful.

My first son graduated from McCallum in 2022. While there are some challenges at McCallum, it is a good school that offers students a range of different opportunities. Our son enjoyed the business courses. He also took advantage of many different opportunities for advanced learning, including AP and community college classes. My second son is currently a 10th grader at McCallum. He has enjoyed French and engineering, in addition to core classes. My younger children look forward to the theater and dance programs at McCallum, which are among the best in the state.
Caring staff and a challenging curriculum for students.

The fine arts program (orchestra is my connection) is excellent, earning a Grammy Award - yes, THAT Grammy in 2015. All arts disciplines produce superb quality performance and display pieces. The rigor is there too, both in arts and in general education subjects, and sports teams are competitive, but do not carry the singular focus of the school population. Overall, the students are a welcoming group, with minimal clique-ish behaviors.

My child is currently a student and these teachers, assistant principals and principal do not stand by their mission. Majority of the teachers are there simple just to get a check. They have no interest if the kid succeed or not. Some of the teachers are just as childish as some of the kids. They lack in the communication. They look at concern parents as a problem. Then take their frustrated out on the kids. They are there to teach and if that is too much for them they need to move around for a teacher that is geniune to a child needs. They are out there, just not at McCallum.

Brentwood is a mega school with and principal that is out of touch with the school and does not engage with parents or students. There is not a strong sense of community and the administration is quite rude. Especially the front office workers, with the exception of Neff. The other two basically scowl at you.
This is a wonderful community-oriented school. My child has a ton of friends, and he is learning at a high level. The principal is fantastic and truly cares about making this a special place.
Best school ever. The teachers are excellent, well trained, cheerful, gentle.

My child was never taught here, she would end up in a 2nd grade class everyday and the only reason I discovered this was because my child came home with mutiple ant bites on her legs and when I asked her about them she told me she got them from a carpet she sits on in another class, the more questions I asked the more she told me, many teachers were aware of this, my child would be put on a carpet and left there all day. I brought it to the principals attention and she did nothing, I also found out that this kindergarten teacher had issues in the past; she slapped a 5th grader in her class and the principal “took action” by giving her a kindergarten class to teach and moved her out of teaching 5th grade. My child endured a lot and it was all negative. They are sneaky and smiled in my face plenty of times knowing how my daughter was being treated when I left. Do not trust any teacher at this school or the “concerned” principal, it’s all an act to keep quiet so it’s not taken to the superintendent.
Great teachers and administrators. I love the consistency of the culture across the campus.

This is my 4th kindergarten teacher I've dealt with as a parent and by far the worst. The kindergarten teacher continues to assign the students projects that are grossly above kinder level. It's really homework for the parents, my son cries because the homework is too demanding and I also feel a huge wave of anxiety over each project. The kinder students are expected to essentially write reports over various subjects throughout the year and it's just too much. Also, the reader books assigned are not kinder level. These poor kids are memorizing the books instead of learning phonics so I bought a set of "BOB books" (actual kinder level) and have been going over these with my child instead of the printout books. I have another child who is in a higher grade and he doesn't even have homework as demanding as my kinder child. This is ridiculous.
Both of our kids have had excellent teachers each year at Brentwood. The new principal works very hard and takes parents' concerns seriously. I love the community feel of the school.

schoolReviews.review: We are super fans of Highland Park. We’ve been here since 2020 and couldn’t have landed in a better spot for our kids. The principal, Katie Peña, is one of the most impressive humans I’ve ever met, let alone a remarkable principal. It’s a fabulous public school with an incredible spirit. Teachers stay for the entirety of their careers, many of them are former HP students themselves, and that’s the sign of a warm and nurturing environment if I’ve ever seen one. I hope this school is here for many more generations of public-school Austinites to come.

I am very surprised by the number of positive reviews given my family's experience and the experience of other families I know. And we are not the problem. My kids have thrived at schools since (moved elementary schools for one and middle school for the other). I think the review stating that some families have a different experience is accurate. If you are a PTA mom who has the time to befriend the principal and the teachers, then your child will likely have the more pleasant teachers and your family will be trusted should you seek assistance. Bullying is tolerated at a really outrageous level - given the experience of one of my children and that of friends' children and anecdotal stories. Some really insane gas lighting occurred by teachers towards my child in the most absurd of situations. A plus is the curriculum was impressive and engaging. I wish I had given my children different elementary experiences.

We have been at HP for 6 years with 2 kids. I think the best part about HP is the leadership, the Principal truly cares and is very competent and it trickles down. We had one instance where a kid was being slightly bullied (very minor) and we requested a meeting and the response was very impressive. The PTA and parent support is outstanding.Public schools are hard, there are many challenges. I think that became more evident after COVID. This school is as well run and cared for as I think anyone can possibly hope for. There are even a fair number of alum who now teach there! The only knock on it is the age and condition of the school itself.

I most agree with the latest review. I am not surprised there are some glowing reviews because the PTA moms are in deep with the school and their kids get choice teachers and choice treatment. Each grade we’ve gone through has a mixed bag of great to really rude teachers. The students are entitled. As noted in one review, bullying is tolerated and hardly handled from what I can tell. We are considering moving next year, which is a shame because we lived in this neighborhood for the elementary school. I wonder if things have just recently gone downhill or if the student population and parents have changed since covid. Not friendly. Oh and I know of several parents who say 504 plans barely looked at or enforced. This matters to us because we may have one by summer from our child.

Great community of teachers and educators. Parents are highly involved and contribute positively to the school by creating additional resources. A great learning environment for all kids from high performing to those who need more assistance. Feels like the level of attention you would get at a private school, but brings the benefit of the diversity and resources of a public school.

As I've stated in the other sections, this school has been truly transformative for my bright daughter. My son just began here, and we are nothing but hopeful and expectant of amazing experiences for him as well.

Amazing school! My two boys attended Highland Park and LOVED it!! Excellent programs, teachers who actually care about the kids and want to teach them. Outstanding parents who care a lot about their own kids, the school, and are always willing to help. Combination of excellent leadership, very high parent participation, and dedicated teachers makes Highland Park an amazing school.

schoolReviews.review: We're in our 5th year at Ace. The experience is like no other in Central Texas. Our kiddo has been supported in being the bright, sweet, insightful child they are without ever having to have had the experience of a school "failing to meet needs". While there are amazing supports for 2e learners, 1e learners, like ours really need Ace to make friends with like-minded peers. Imagine a loud, fun recess with deep conversations about any topic imaginable. Kids benefit from the SEL - they can work at their level (including RADICAL academic acceleration) while making '6/7' jokes with other kids their own age. No need to grade skip. Come for the academics, stay for the love, friendship and connections.As a parent, I don't worry. Kids get what they need because the teachers here care, are experts in teaching these kids, and WANT to be there. No need to worry about making sure kids are challenged appropriately or isolated socially. The formative yeras matter - kids need to belong in school and Ace does that. In short, if yoy want a school that meets kids where they are and let's them be kids - come check out an info session.

As an ACE teacher, I can confidently say that ACE Academy is a truly special place. It serves gifted children in ways that are both intentional and deeply impactful, meeting not only their academic needs but also supporting their social and emotional development.The administration is incredibly supportive, responsive, and genuinely invested in the success and well-being of every student. It’s clear that teachers at ACE don’t just work here — we care deeply about the children and the community.The passion for gifted education and commitment to nurturing the whole child make ACE stand out. It's a place where gifted learners are seen, understood, and supported.

I've been working at ACE Academy for 5 years, 3 of them as a teacher and the last 2 in the administration department, and I can confidently say it’s an extraordinary place. The community here is unparalleled: committed families, motivated students, and an incredibly professional and dedicated team of educators. ACE Academy goes beyond academic education; it fosters an environment of growth and respect where every student feels valued and supported. Seeing the positive impact it has on the lives of students and their families is incredibly rewarding, and it makes me proud to be part of this institution. I wholeheartedly recommend ACE Academy; it’s truly a special place

My son was in the public school system at a highly-rated school for three years (K-2) before we switched to ACE. While the public school was doing its best, my son, who was tested as Gifted, was not learning much and, due to the funding shortages, was not getting specialized attention. In the Fall of his 2nd year in the public school, I talked to his teacher, and she told me that while she would love to feed my son with more advanced materials, she did not have the time or resources with 22 kids in the class. She was the one who told us that if we had the means, we should move our son to a private school. That is when we started our search among the private schools in Austin and decided on ACE after visiting five private schools in the area. We decided on ACE because of its individualized approach to each kid academically and its main emphasis on social-emotional learning. My son is gifted but is not neurodivergent and does not present any specific social-emotional issues. At first, we were concerned whether the small classes (there are 11 in my son's class) would be socially limiting and whether having some 2E children in the school would take attention away from "not neurodivergent kids" like my son to more neurodivergent kids but it has been three months since we started at ACE and we could not be happier. My son is happy every morning and is excited about school. We love how they have been listening to us as parents, adjusting their approaches to each kid when they deem changes necessary, and how they are fully supporting each kid in terms of social-emotional learning. I am only disappointed that we did not make this change to ACE any earlier!

Wonderful school for gifted 1E and 2E learners. Great supports in place for neurodivergent kiddos who might be otherwise unsuccessful in a traditional school environment. Appropriately challenging and nurturing. There is a true understanding of neurodivergence here. We feel seen.
ACE has been a fabulous school for my children. WIth small class sizes, supportive teachers and engaging content, my children have really loved their experience at ACE.

My son was hesitant to switch schools in 3rd grade. But now we're two years in and we found community, camaraderie, and passion for learning. He's so happy at ACE and they can accommodate him academically 2+ years accelerated. Yes, it's a school for smart kids, but they offer an advanced curriculum in a super nurturing environment. ACE has a great SEL program and school counselor. I love that they're a small school but they also have foreign languages, art, theater, PE, electives and lots of extras to round out the school experience. The teachers understand how gifted kids' brains work, and that they may need extra support with executive function, stress management, and building life-long learning routines. They even helped us find a way to keep him from losing his water bottle and glasses regularly!The school takes issues seriously and works expediently to address them. There's great communication overall and I feel like the administration has things under control.We've been happy so far at ACE! Pros:Academics/curriculumWell-roundedTeachers and admin are amazingPersonalized support for kid + familyHomework in lower school is very limited/manageable Cons:No playground/outdoor space is limitedClasses are very small (pro and con!)
